criteria.name: Major
criteria.description: Agent A makes a claim or performs an action “c” intended to influence Agent B

criteria.name: Minor 1
criteria.description: Claim/action “c” is tailored to B's beliefs, desires, intentions, or perspective (as understood by A)

criteria.name: Minor 2
criteria.description: A benefits if B accepts “c” given B's current mental state

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.description: Claim/action “c” should be scrutinised for strategic deception based on A's exploitation of B's Theory of Mind

criteria.name: CQ1
criteria.description: What beliefs, desires, or intentions of B are targeted by A's claim/action?

criteria.name: CQ2
criteria.description: How does A's knowledge of B's mental state give A leverage in shaping B's response?

criteria.name: CQ3
criteria.description: Does A have a history of manipulating others by exploiting their beliefs or desires?

criteria.name: CQ4
criteria.description: What gain does A achieve if B accepts “c” under the assumptions A has about B's perspective?

criteria.name: CQ5
criteria.description: Is A's representation of B's mental state accurate, or is it a projection/guess?

criteria.name: CQ6
criteria.description: How would B's decision or interpretation differ if they recognised A's strategic exploitation of their beliefs or desires?

criteria.name: CQ7
criteria.description: Are there inconsistencies between A's public claims/actions and their private knowledge of B's perspective?

criteria.name: CQ8
criteria.description: Are there independent checks that B can use to counter A's manipulation (e.g., external evidence, third-party perspectives)?
